metadata.title: Consumer Neuroscience Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary papers and references for 12 consumer-neuroscience primitives: attention & salience, arousal physiology, social bonding, narrative transportation, approach-avoidance, mirror systems, neuroaesthetics, interoception, memory consolidation, reward anticipation, embodied cognition, predictive processing.

primary_papers.name: A Feature-Integration Theory of Attention
primary_papers.description: Treisman, A. M. & Gelade, G. (1980). Cognitive Psychology, 12(1), 97–136. Foundational Feature Integration Theory; pre-attentive feature detection and the distinction between automatic feature pop-out and serial search. Primary source for primitive #1 (attention & salience).

primary_papers.name: Computational Modelling of Visual Attention
primary_papers.description: Itti, L. & Koch, C. (2001). Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2(3), 194–203. Computational salience maps formalizing bottom-up attentional priority. Primary source for primitive #1 (attention & salience).

primary_papers.name: How to Conduct Valuable Marketing Research With Neurophysiological Tools
primary_papers.description: Bigne, E. et al. (2025). Psychology & Marketing. Comprehensive methodological review of neurophysiological tools (EEG, GSR, eye-tracking, fMRI, facial EMG) in consumer research; 2025 empirical anchor for primitives #1 (attention), #2 (arousal), and #6 (mirror systems).

primary_papers.name: The Relation of Strength of Stimulus to Rapidity of Habit-Formation
primary_papers.description: Yerkes, R. M. & Dodson, J. D. (1908). Journal of Comparative Neurology and Psychology, 18(5), 459–482. Foundational Yerkes-Dodson law; inverted-U relationship between arousal and performance. Primary source for primitive #2 (arousal physiology).

primary_papers.name: Physiology and Neurobiology of Stress and Adaptation
primary_papers.description: McEwen, B. S. (2007). Physiological Reviews, 87(3), 873–904. Allostatic load model; sustained autonomic activation as physiological cost. Primary source for primitive #2 (arousal physiology).

primary_papers.name: Neuro-Insights: A Systematic Review of Neuromarketing Perspectives Across Consumer Buying Stages
primary_papers.description: Frontiers in Neuroergonomics (11 July 2025). DOI: 10.3389/fnrgo.2025.1542847. Systematic review of neuromarketing tools and findings across pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase stages. SOR framing. 2025 empirical anchor for primitives #2 (arousal), #4 (narrative), and composition recipes.

primary_papers.name: The Moral Molecule
primary_papers.description: Zak, P. J. (2012). The Moral Molecule. Dutton. Oxytocin, trust, and prosocial economic behavior; narrative as oxytocin trigger. Primary source for primitive #3 (social bonding).

primary_papers.name: Oxytocin Pathways and the Evolution of Human Behavior
primary_papers.description: Carter, C. S. (2014). Annual Review of Psychology, 65, 17–39. Evolutionary depth of oxytocin affiliative circuits; bonding, parental care, and social group cohesion. Primary source for primitive #3 (social bonding).

primary_papers.name: The Role of Transportation in the Persuasiveness of Public Narratives
primary_papers.description: Green, M. C. & Brock, T. C. (2000). Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 79(5), 701–721. Foundational transportation theory; transportation score predicts attitude change and belief formation. Primary source for primitive #4 (narrative transportation).

primary_papers.name: The Brain's Default Network
primary_papers.description: Buckner, R. L., Andrews-Hanna, J. R. & Schacter, D. L. (2008). Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, 1124(1), 1–38. Default Mode Network and self-referential processing; vmPFC role in narrative absorption. Primary source for primitive #4 (narrative transportation).

primary_papers.name: xAI/fMRI Approaches to Brand Narrative and Default-Mode Processing
primary_papers.description: Frontiers in Human Neuroscience (2024). fMRI evidence on brand-narrative alignment with default-mode network processing and downstream brand preference. 2024 empirical anchor for primitive #4 (narrative transportation).

primary_papers.name: Beyond Pleasure and Pain
primary_papers.description: Higgins, E. T. (1997). American Psychologist, 52(12), 1280–1300. Foundational regulatory focus theory; promotion vs prevention orientation. Primary source for primitive #5 (approach-avoidance).

primary_papers.name: Behavioral Inhibition, Behavioral Activation, and Affective Responses to Impending Reward and Punishment
primary_papers.description: Carver, C. S. & White, T. L. (1994). Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(2), 319–333. BIS/BAS scale and behavioral evidence; reward vs threat sensitivity dissociation. Primary source for primitive #5 (approach-avoidance).

primary_papers.name: The Mirror-Neuron System
primary_papers.description: Rizzolatti, G. & Craighero, L. (2004). Annual Review of Neuroscience, 27, 169–192. Foundational mirror neuron system review; motor simulation of observed actions. Primary source for primitive #6 (mirror systems).

primary_papers.name: Emotional Contagion
primary_papers.description: Hatfield, E., Cacioppo, J. T. & Rapson, R. L. (1993). Current Directions in Psychological Science, 2(3), 96–99. Foundational emotional contagion; automatic mirroring of observed emotional expressions. Primary source for primitive #6 (mirror systems).

primary_papers.name: The Science of Art: A Neurological Theory of Aesthetic Experience
primary_papers.description: Ramachandran, V. S. & Hirstein, W. (1999). Journal of Consciousness Studies, 6(6–7), 15–51. Foundational neuroaesthetics; peak-shift principle; eight laws of artistic experience. Primary source for primitive #7 (neuroaesthetics).

primary_papers.name: The Aesthetic Brain
primary_papers.description: Chatterjee, A. (2014). The Aesthetic Brain. Oxford University Press. Neural basis of visual beauty; ventral pathway and aesthetic reward; symmetry and contour processing. Primary source for primitive #7 (neuroaesthetics).

primary_papers.name: Descartes' Error
primary_papers.description: Damasio, A. R. (1996). Descartes' Error. Papermac. Somatic marker hypothesis; vmPFC integration of body-state signals into pre-deliberative decision bias. Primary source for primitive #8 (interoception & somatic markers).

primary_papers.name: How Do You Feel — Now? The Anterior Insula and Human Awareness
primary_papers.description: Craig, A. D. (2009). Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 10(1), 59–70. Anterior insula as the primary cortical substrate for interoception; meta-interoception and subjective feeling states. Primary source for primitive #8 (interoception & somatic markers).

primary_papers.name: The Organization of Behavior
primary_papers.description: Hebb, D. O. (1949). The Organization of Behavior. Wiley. Hebbian synaptic potentiation; the foundational mechanism for experience-dependent neural plasticity and learning. Primary source for primitive #9 (memory consolidation).

primary_papers.name: Why We Sleep
primary_papers.description: Walker, M. P. (2017). Why We Sleep. Scribner. Sleep-dependent hippocampal replay; NREM slow-wave consolidation; sleep disruption effects on memory formation. Primary source for primitive #9 (memory consolidation).

primary_papers.name: Anticipation of Increasing Monetary Reward Selectively Recruits Nucleus Accumbens
primary_papers.description: Knutson, B., Adams, C. M., Fong, G. W. & Hommer, D. (2001). Journal of Neuroscience, 21(16), RC159. Nucleus accumbens activation during reward anticipation; wanting signal peaks before reward delivery. Primary source for primitive #10 (reward anticipation).

primary_papers.name: The Debate Over Dopamine's Role in Reward: The Case for Incentive Salience
primary_papers.description: Berridge, K. C. (2007). Psychopharmacology, 191(3), 391–431. Wanting/liking dissociation; incentive salience theory; mesolimbic dopamine as wanting signal distinct from hedonic liking. Primary source for primitive #10 (reward anticipation).

primary_papers.name: Philosophy in the Flesh
primary_papers.description: Lakoff, G. & Johnson, M. (1999). Philosophy in the Flesh. Basic Books. Conceptual metaphor theory; sensorimotor grounding of abstract thought; embodied cognition. Primary source for primitive #11 (embodied cognition).

primary_papers.name: Grounded Cognition
primary_papers.description: Barsalou, L. W. (2008). Annual Review of Psychology, 59, 617–645. Perceptual symbol systems; grounded simulation of concepts through partial sensorimotor reenactment. Primary source for primitive #11 (embodied cognition).

primary_papers.name: The Free-Energy Principle: A Unified Brain Theory?
primary_papers.description: Friston, K. (2010). Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 11(2), 127–138. Free-energy minimization as the unifying computational principle of brain function; predictive processing. Primary source for primitive #12 (predictive processing).

primary_papers.name: Whatever Next? Predictive Brains, Situated Agents, and the Future of Cognitive Science
primary_papers.description: Clark, A. (2013). Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 36(3), 181–204. Active inference; predictive processing as unifying cognitive science framework; design implications for prediction-error management. Primary source for primitive #12 (predictive processing).

primary_papers.name: Extended Active Inference
primary_papers.description: Constant, A., Clark, A., Kirchhoff, M. & Friston, K. (2019). Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B, 374. Active inference extended beyond the skull; niche construction; product design shapes user world-models. Source for primitive #12 (predictive processing).

primary_papers.name: Predictive Processing: A Review
primary_papers.description: Sprevak, M. (2024). Topics in Cognitive Science; and (2025) Inquiry. Current state of predictive processing theory; scope of evidence and applied range. 2024/2025 empirical anchor for primitive #12 (predictive processing).

primary_papers.name: Neuromarketing and the Marketing Mix: An Integrative Review and Future Research Agenda Using the TMC Approach
primary_papers.description: Bansal, A. et al. (2025). International Journal of Consumer Studies. Integrative review of neuromarketing across the marketing mix using the TMC approach; SOR framing. 2025 empirical anchor for composition recipes and Frontiers neuro-insights cross-reference.

primary_papers.name: Noninvasive Neuromarketing Methods: An Overview
primary_papers.description: F1000Research 14:1132 (2024). Overview of noninvasive neuromarketing measurement methods (EEG, fMRI, fNIRS, GSR, eye-tracking, facial EMG); methodological limitations and ethical constraints. Cross-reference for primitives #2, #6, and #8.

primary_papers.name: A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward
primary_papers.description: Schultz, W., Dayan, P. & Montague, P. R. (1997). Science, 275(5306), 1593–1599. VTA dopamine neurons as prediction-error signals; ~200ms anticipatory onset before conditioned cue. Cross-reference for primitive #10 (reward anticipation) and #12 (predictive processing).

primary_papers.name: Oxytocin and Social Reward: Is There a Link?
primary_papers.description: Ott, V. et al. (2013). Frontiers in Neuroscience, 7, 264. Oxytocin plasma half-life ~3–5 minutes; social reward circuitry; implications for session-level warmth design. Source for primitive #3 (social bonding).

primary_papers.name: A neurofunctional signature of affective arousal generalizes across valence domains and distinguishes subjective experience from autonomic reactivity
primary_papers.description: Nature Communications (July 14, 2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-61706-0. Discovery n=60/36; validation across 24 studies, n=868. Identifies a brain affective arousal signature (BAAS) in distributed cortical-subcortical systems (prefrontal, PAG, thalamo-amygdala-insula). BAAS generalizes across valence (positive and negative) and is statistically distinct from autonomic arousal (GSR/HRV) and from wakefulness. Key CORRECT for primitive #2: GSR/autonomic signals do not fully proxy subjective affective arousal.

primary_papers.name: A registered replication study on oxytocin and trust
primary_papers.description: Declerck, C. H., Boone, C., Pauwels, L., Vogt, B., & Fehr, E. (2020). Nature Human Behaviour, 4, 646–655. Registered pre-registered replication with >95% power. No main effect of intranasal oxytocin on trusting behavior under standard social conditions. Exploratory: possible effect in low-trust-disposition individuals. Required qualification for primitive #3 (social bonding) — the simple oxytocin=trust narrative is overclaiming.

primary_papers.name: Reliability of EEG Metrics for Assessing Video Advertisements
primary_papers.description: Journal of Advertising (2024/2025 online first). DOI: 10.1080/00913367.2024.2418109. n=116 participants, 13 TV commercials. ISC is the most reliable EEG metric for ad testing (n≈11–15 for r=0.7 reliability). Alpha, beta, gamma, theta reliability improve with repetition. Alpha-asymmetry reliability does not improve with additional viewings — a key limitation for its use in neuromarketing. Key update for primitives #1 and #2.

primary_papers.name: Intersubject correlation as a predictor of attention: a systematic review
primary_papers.description: BMC Psychology (2025). DOI: 10.1186/s40359-025-02879-7. PMC: PMC12100797. 14 studies, 27 effect sizes. Meta-analytic estimate r=0.65 (p<0.001) for ISC as neural marker of attentional engagement. Covers naturalistic stimuli (video clips) and controlled tasks. Corroborates ISC as the highest-reliability neuromarketing EEG metric. Key update for primitive #1 (attention).

primary_papers.name: A comprehensive evaluation framework for consumer-grade EEG devices: signal quality, robustness, and usability
primary_papers.description: Scientific Reports (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-39056-8. n=30 participants, 4 consumer-grade EEG devices (BrainLink Pro, NeuroNicle FX2, Mindwave Mobile2, Muse2) vs DSI-24 research-grade reference. P300 detectable in consumer devices but ERP temporal pattern distorted. Muse2 shows poorest signal quality (broadband power distortion, highest test-retest variability). Consumer devices more artifact-prone in frontal region. Key qualification for primitive #1 and #2 instrumentation claims.

primary_papers.name: EEG dataset of consumer- and research-grade systems
primary_papers.description: Scientific Data (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-06962-5. PMC: PMC13076875. Public dataset from the same consumer vs. research-grade EEG evaluation study (Finding 3). Enables cross-study validation and standardization of consumer EEG claims. Corroborating source for consumer EEG qualification.

primary_papers.name: Inferring mental states from neuroimaging data
primary_papers.description: Poldrack, R. A. (2011). Neuron, 72(5), 692–697. DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2011.11.001. Foundational critique of reverse inference in neuroimaging: inferring a mental state from observed brain activation requires a highly selective mapping between state and region — a condition rarely met. Landmark paper in neuromarketing methodology; anchors the ML-ON-NEURO REVERSE INFERENCE TRAP and the Anti-Frameworks ML-classifier-as-mind-reader entry in frameworks-meta.md.

primary_papers.name: Predicting advertising preference using machine learning on EDA and facial action
primary_papers.description: Marques et al. (2025). Psychology & Marketing, 42(1), 175–192. DOI: 10.1002/mar.22118. Random Forest model on EDA + facial action coding unit (FEA) data achieves 81% accuracy and 81% F1 for predicting ad preference. Single-lab result; not yet replicated across independent stimulus sets. Evidence grade: B — promising but treat as lab-specific until cross-validated. Anchors ML-ON-NEURO OVERFIT trap in patterns-scenarios-traps.md.

primary_papers.name: ML/DL in Neuromarketing Research — Editorial and Research Topic
primary_papers.description: Frontiers in Human Neuroscience (2025). DOI: 10.3389/fnhum.2025.1638225. PMC: PMC12230022. Editorial summarising 8 contributions on ML and DL in consumer neuroscience research. Identifies reverse inference and small-N overfitting as two persistent challenges ML is claimed to resolve but does not; ML changes the surface form of reverse inference (trained prior) rather than eliminating it. Evidence grade: B — peer-reviewed synthesis; no direct empirical test of the ML-vs-reverse-inference claim. Anchors ML-ON-NEURO REVERSE INFERENCE TRAP and Anti-Frameworks row in frameworks-meta.md.

primary_papers.name: Neuroforecasting reveals generalizable components of choice
primary_papers.description: Genevsky, A., Tong, L. C., & Knutson, B. (2025). PNAS Nexus, 4(2), pgaf029. DOI: 10.1093/pnasnexus/pgaf029. Two-experiment fMRI study showing NAcc activity (early affective response) forecasts aggregate internet-market choices regardless of lab-sample demographic representativeness; MPFC does not generalize. Sample ~20–25 subjects sufficient for reliable forecast. Key update for primitive #10 (reward anticipation) and neuroforecasting applications.

primary_papers.name: Brain activity reveals how wildlife imagery evokes engagement on social media
primary_papers.description: Srirangarajan, T., Sawe, N., Thys, T., Wu, X. C., & Knutson, B. (2026). PNAS Nexus, 5(2), pgag012. n=34. Group MPFC activity forecast aggregate social-media engagement (National Geographic Instagram) out-of-sample; NAcc and MPFC both predicted individual liking and donations. Domain-dependent result: in conservation/social-media domain MPFC (not NAcc) generalised to aggregate — distinct from Genevsky 2025 (commercial markets, NAcc → aggregate). Together the two papers establish that the region forecasting aggregate is domain-dependent.

regulatory_sources.name: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
regulatory_sources.description: UK primary legislation. In force 6 April 2025. Restates and extends CPRs 2008 consumer protection provisions. CMA direct civil enforcement; fines up to 10% of global annual turnover. Online choice architecture and dark patterns directly actionable. Relevant to all primitives via ethical bounds sections.

regulatory_sources.name: CMA DMCC Act Procedural Guidance — April 2025
regulatory_sources.description: CMA (April 2025). Procedural guidance on enforcement powers under the DMCC Act 2024. Establishes CMA investigation and enforcement process. Relevant to ethical bounds, misuse boundaries across all primitives.

regulatory_sources.name: CMA Price Transparency Guidance — December 2025
regulatory_sources.description: CMA (December 2025). Guidance on price transparency requirements under DMCC Act 2024; drip pricing and incremental price reveal addressed. Relevant to primitive #2 (manufactured arousal via pricing pressure) and composition recipes.

regulatory_sources.name: CMA First DMCC Enforcement Actions — 18 November 2025
regulatory_sources.description: CMA (18 November 2025). First enforcement actions under DMCC Act 2024 against 8 firms; drip pricing, default opt-ins, pressure selling. ~100 advisory letters across 14 sectors. Directly referenced in SKILL.md UK Regulatory Context section.

regulatory_sources.name: ASA CAP Code (Non-Broadcast Advertising)
regulatory_sources.description: ASA/CAP (current). Non-broadcast advertising standards; misleading claims, false testimonials, fabricated social proof, manufactured urgency. Relevant to primitives #6 (mirror systems/testimonials) and #3 (social bonding/fabricated warmth).

regulatory_sources.name: ICO Guidance on Biometric Data and Special Category Processing
regulatory_sources.description: ICO / UK GDPR (current). Special-category data; Article 9 explicit consent requirements for biometric and physiological measurement (GSR, HRV, eye-tracking, facial EMG, EEG). Directly relevant to DMCC compliance audit recipe and primitives #2, #6, and #8 misuse boundaries.

regulatory_sources.name: Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008
regulatory_sources.description: UK statutory instrument. Aggressive and misleading commercial practices; now restated and extended within DMCC Act 2024. Historical anchor for dark-pattern analysis; provisions relevant to manufactured urgency and pressure-selling primitives.

regulatory_sources.name: Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness
regulatory_sources.description: Thaler, R. H. & Sunstein, C. R. (2008). Yale University Press. Harm test for nudge vs dark pattern; choice architecture ethics. Applied as the ethical frame across all primitives in SKILL.md and primitives-overview.md.

regulatory_sources.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
regulatory_sources.description: EU primary legislation. Article 5 prohibitions in force 2 February 2025: subliminal/manipulative AI techniques causing significant harm; exploitation of vulnerabilities (age, disability, socio-economic). Workplace and education emotion-recognition prohibited. Article 50 transparency obligations for emotion-recognition and biometric-categorisation systems. Annex III high-risk classification covers commercial emotion recognition. Directly relevant to Ethical Bounds EU section and primitives #2, #3, #6, #8 misuse boundaries.

regulatory_sources.name: EU AI Act High-Risk System Obligations — In Force 2 August 2026
regulatory_sources.description: EU AI Act Article 6 + Annex III. From 2 August 2026, high-risk AI systems including commercial emotion-recognition and biometric-categorisation must meet data governance, technical documentation, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, and post-market monitoring requirements. Any consumer product using AI to infer affect from facial expression, voice, GSR, HRV, eye-tracking, or fNIRS must be compliant. Anchors the May 2026 readiness window referenced in SKILL.md EU Regulatory Context.

regulatory_sources.name: EU AI Act Article 5 — Prohibited AI Practices
regulatory_sources.description: EU AI Act Article 5. Prohibited practices include subliminal techniques beyond consciousness, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques causing significant harm, and exploitation of vulnerabilities (age, disability, socio-economic). In force 2 February 2025. Directly captures the manipulation column of the SKILL.md ethics table when AI is in the loop. Reinforces the Vulnerable-User Note alongside DMCC enforcement priorities.

regulatory_sources.name: California SB 1223 — Neural Data as CCPA Sensitive Personal Information
regulatory_sources.description: California SB 1223 (signed 28 Sep 2024; effective 1 Jan 2025). Amends CCPA to include 'neural data' — signals from central or peripheral nervous system — as sensitive personal information. Requires separate opt-in consent; right to delete and restrict sharing apply. Directly relevant to any consumer product capturing EEG, GSR, eye-tracking, facial coding, or voice-affect signals served to California users. Anchors the US Regulatory Context section in SKILL.md and US Neural Data Laws gate in ethics-operational-checklist.md.

regulatory_sources.name: Colorado HB 24-1058 — Neural Data Under Colorado Privacy Act
regulatory_sources.description: Colorado HB 24-1058 (signed April 2024; effective 7 August 2024). Amends Colorado Privacy Act to include 'neural data' within 'biological data' as a category of sensitive data. First US law to define and protect neural data specifically. Requires opt-in consent for processing. Anchors the US Regulatory Context section in SKILL.md.

regulatory_sources.name: Connecticut SB 1295 — Neural Data Under CTDPA
regulatory_sources.description: Connecticut SB 1295 (signed 24 June 2025; effective 1 July 2026). Amends Connecticut Data Privacy Act to add neural data as a sensitive data category. Express consumer consent required for processing; selling sensitive data without consent prohibited. Processing thresholds removed for sensitive data. Anchors the US Regulatory Context section in SKILL.md and US Neural Data Laws gate in ethics-operational-checklist.md.

regulatory_sources.name: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology
regulatory_sources.description: UNESCO General Conference, 43rd session (adopted 12 November 2025). First global non-binding ethical framework for neurotechnology covering neural data across commercial uses. Principles include mental privacy, transparency, consent, human dignity, and protection of vulnerable groups. Non-binding but widely cited in board-level compliance discussions and DPA engagement. Anchors the US/global Regulatory Context section in SKILL.md.

regulatory_sources.name: Oxytocin increases trust in humans with a low disposition to trust (bioRxiv 2025, preprint)
regulatory_sources.description: bioRxiv preprint (2025; DOI: 10.1101/2025.10.01.679711). Preregistered high-powered study. Oxytocin administration increased trusting behaviour by ~15%; pooled analysis (low-trusting individuals) yielded ~16.9% increase. Selective effect in low-trust-disposition individuals. Note: PREPRINT — not yet peer-reviewed; treat as preliminary. Cited in SKILL.md Fact-Checking #3 (social bonding) oxytocin replication note. Context: the Declerck 2020 registered replication (peer-reviewed, Nature Human Behaviour) found no main effect; this preprint provides a qualified positive result under restricted conditions. Both must be cited together.

regulatory_sources.name: Vermont H.814 / Act 101 — Neurological Rights Statement, No Consent Gate (corrected)
regulatory_sources.description: Vermont H.814 / Act 101 (signed 18 May 2026; effective 1 July 2026). CORRECTED: the enacted act was substantially narrowed in the Senate — the consent requirement and private right of action were stripped before passage. It recognises a largely declaratory 'neurological rights' statement (mental privacy, freedom of thought, non-discrimination in neurotechnology) with enforcement resting exclusively with the Vermont Attorney General, and commissions a study reporting to the next legislative session. No consent gate for businesses. Vermont's binding neural-data framework is S.71 (neural data as sensitive data), effective 1 January 2028. Do not cite H.814 as an active consent gate. Anchors the corrected US Regulatory Context section in SKILL.md and US Neural Data Laws gate in ethics-operational-checklist.md.
